26b4934d4ac7:
Icon on glass ”The Coronation of the Mother of God” – model: Transylvanian workshop (Mărginimea Sibiului), mid-19th century

This theme of Western inspiration (also known as “the Coronation of the Virgin”) is depicted (in the icon I am suggesting to you today as a special gift idea) as the New Testament Holy Trinity crowning the Mother of God. Sometimes this theme was classed under “the Holy Trinity” or “the Holy Trinity with the Coronation of the Virgin”.

About the icon: the Heavenly Father holds a sceptre in one hand, and Jesus holds the cross of the crucifixion. Above the head of the Virgin Mary, in the upper register, the Holy Spirit is shown in the form of a dove. The iconographic theme is accompanied by angels in the upper and lower registers. The scene of "the Coronation of the Mother of God" is an iconographic depiction of the dogma of the immaculate conception, according to which the Mother of God is above the heavenly order.

47ea99b458c4:
Saint Paraskeva – icon on glass
A traditional Romanian icon made after a Nicula model (18th century), respecting the techniques of this art form. This icon is perfect as an unusual gift, for its theme, its small size
~12x17 cm (without frame); 20x25 cm (with frame)~ and its decorative frame with a stand on the back.

The theme of this icon is Saint Paraskeva the New, or Paraskeva of Iași, a venerable saint honoured throughout the Orthodox Church, especially in Romania, Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria. In Romania she is considered the protector of Moldavia and is the most popular of all the saints whose relics lie on Romanian soil. Hundreds of parish churches in Romania are dedicated to her, for her protection. Among the people she is also known as Saint Friday. Her feast is on 14 October, when tens of thousands of people come to Iași every year to venerate her holy relics.

23cbd27b786b:
~Saint Nikephoros the Leper, with scenes from his life~

The icon (my own composition) is not available; it will be painted again only to order. The icon I am showing you today is painted on glass (30x42 cm) in the traditional technique.

Doxologia.ro:
The Venerable Nikephoros the Leper was born on the island of Crete into a family of devout peasants and was orphaned at an early age. At thirteen, the first signs of the “holy disease”, as leprosy is called in the Church of Christ, appeared on his body. To escape the permanent isolation that awaited him, he took refuge for a time in Egypt. At twenty-four he arrived at the leper colony on Chios, in the care of Saint Anthimos of Chios, where he was tonsured a monk. There, for forty-one years, although more and more crippled by the disease, he gave himself with a martyr's patience to struggles beyond nature, becoming an example for his brothers in suffering.
After the cure for leprosy was discovered in 1947, the leper colony on Chios was closed and the Venerable one was moved to the Saint Barbara Hospital in Athens. Blind and confined to his sickbed, yet endowed with many divine gifts, he spent the last years of his life giving hope to the despairing, comfort to the suffering and zeal to the young. At the age of seventy-four the holy leper departed this world; later, the finding of his holy relics and the countless healings he still works today showed him to be one of the greatest intercessors of our times.
In 2012 the Ecumenical Patriarchate glorified Saint Nikephoros the Leper, with his feast on 4 January, the day of his falling asleep.

114b05d30890:
Saint Stylianos of Paphlagonia
The Church celebrates Saint STYLIANOS OF PAPHLAGONIA on 26 November. He was born in the 6th century, in Adrianople. His family was very rich, but he gave up all his wealth and became a monk. So Saint Stylianos went into the wilderness, to prayer and fasting. An angel brought him food every day in the cave where he lived. After a while, a merciless disease began to kill the children of the people of that land. The people turned to Saint STYLIANOS to intercede with God. And so the children of many were healed, and those whose babies had already died were soon able to have others. For this reason Saint STYLIANOS is considered the protector of children, especially of infants, and a great help to parents of sick children. In iconography he is shown holding a baby in his arms.
This icon painted on glass is not available (it is in a holy and beautiful Church); it will be painted to order.
